pins.title: One Tight Spot or Lingering Stiffness? Massage Gun vs Red Light Panel
pins.subtitle: Match the tool to your soreness
pins.description: A specific knot after a workout fits a massage gun's targeted, on-demand approach. General stiffness that builds over a training block may suit a red light panel, if you'll realistically do 10 to 20 minute sessions several times a week. Neither replaces sleep or rest days. Pacemaker, pregnant, or a skin or clotting condition? Ask a doctor first. Not medical advice. #massagegun #redlighttherapy #musclerecovery #homerecovery

pins.title: Red Light Therapy vs Massage Gun: What the Research Does and Doesn't Show
pins.subtitle: An honest look at the evidence
pins.description: Both get marketed with more confidence than the research supports. Small studies suggest massage guns may ease how sore you feel. Red light results vary with power output, wavelength, and distance, and home panels differ from clinical devices. Treat both as possible supporting habits, not fixes. Not medical advice. #redlighttherapy #massagegun #recoveryscience #percussivetherapy #photobiomodulation

pins.title: A 2-Minute Tool vs a 20-Minute Habit: Massage Gun or Red Light Panel?
pins.subtitle: Gym bag or a fixed spot at home
pins.description: A massage gun lives in a gym bag and works in short bursts on one muscle group. A red light panel needs a fixed spot at home, like a bedroom corner or home gym, and a session of 10 to 20 minutes that pays off over weeks, not one use. Pick the one you'll actually stick with. Not medical advice. #massagegun #redlightpanel #recoveryroutine #homegym #postworkout
